newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel hits all-time low against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel hits all-time low against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel fell to an all-time low against the dollar on Monday ahead of the Bank of Israel announcement on February interest rates, dealers said.

"Trading was very quiet today as investors waited for the rate decision. Investors expected a minimal cut of 0.5 percentage point or less. Such a cut will have no impact on the local forex market," said Guy Levi at Bank Leumi.
The Bank of Israel announced a 0.5-point cut to 14.2 percent after the representative rate had been fixed.
"During the day the shekel moved in a very narrow range despite the rise of the dollar abroad," Levi added. "The basket fell once more to more than seven percent below the diagonal rate."

The shekel is allowed to fluctuate in a trading band of seven percent above or below a sloping mid-point designed to devalue the Israeli currency at a rate of six percent a year against the basket of key currencies.
Dealers said the Bank of Israel intervened in the market several times buying dollars on a relatively small scale to support the basket.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3060 shekels against 3.3000 shekels on Friday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6247 shekels against 3.6240 on Friday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.7695 shekels per 100 yen against 2.7699 on Friday and against the mark at 2.0175 shekels against 2.0212 on Friday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.3010 shekels.
